evidence: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30-32 builds the denial key as namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent, with no escaping or length prefixes. pkg/util/shortid_generator.go:32-34 allows '_' in UIDs (a-zA-Z0-9-_), so two different (name, parent) pairs can produce the same key. Example: name="a_b", parent="c" and name="a", parent="b_c" both give "..._a_b_c". pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116-121 returns Allowed:false on any denial-cache hit without re-checking, and service.go:153-155 writes the key after a deny. So a deny for one resource can wrongly deny a different resource for the same user and action. The impact is small: the failure is fail-closed (a wrong deny, never a wrong allow), the entry expires after shortCacheTTL = 30s (service.go:32), and it needs two UIDs that happen to line up this way. Still, a wrong 30s deny is exactly the 'creator can't access what they just created' symptom this PR is fixing, and the fix is cheap: escape the segments or use a delimiter UIDs can't contain.
